_note: DEMO CONTENT. This file is the fixture the whole test matrix leans on — /tests/index.html and both MCP walkthroughs load it. Subject matter is deliberately general-knowledge, public-domain, and fictional-where-invented: the repo is public and carries no identifiable or regulated data, ever. Jeopardy convention is honored throughout: `prompt` is a statement, `answer` is phrased as a question. Point values come from each column's `valueLadder` by position (plan Q8: cells[i] takes valueLadder[i]); one cell below carries an explicit `value` to exercise the per-cell override. This whole key is a comment and is stripped by the validator (spec §2.4).
title: Quiz Board Engine Demo — General Knowledge

columns._note: A second comment, nested one level down, proving _note is legal at every object level and not just at the root.
columns.label: World Capitals

cells.prompt: This city on the Seine has been the capital of France since the Middle Ages.
Japan's capital took its modern name in 1868; before that it was called Edo.
In 1960 Brazil moved its capital inland to this purpose-built city.
This Bhutanese capital is often called the only world capital with no traffic lights.
Kazakhstan's capital has changed names repeatedly; it went back to this one in 2022.
This king of the Greek gods ruled from Olympus and threw thunderbolts.
This hero's twelve labours began with strangling the lion of Nemea.
This Norse trickster fathered the wolf Fenrir and engineered Balder's death.
This Egyptian goddess gathered up the scattered pieces of her husband Osiris.
In the Mesopotamian epic, this wild man of the steppe becomes Gilgamesh's closest friend.
Element number one, and by far the most abundant element in the universe.
This metal's symbol, Fe, comes from its Latin name ferrum.
This noble gas glows orange-red in a discharge tube and lent its name to bright signs.
Liquid at room temperature, this metal was once known as quicksilver.
Element 79 takes its symbol, Au, from the Latin aurum.
This Danish prince wonders aloud whether to be, or not to be.
Two households, both alike in dignity, feud through this Verona tragedy.
Three witches on a heath greet this Scottish thane with a prophecy.
This aging king divides his kingdom among his daughters, with catastrophic results.
Shipwrecked and exiled to an island, this magician commands the spirit Ariel.
The largest animal known to have lived, it strains krill through plates of baleen.
This eight-armed mollusc changes colour and squeezes through impossibly small gaps.
The deepest known point in any ocean lies at the bottom of this Pacific trench.
These colonial animals build reefs from calcium carbonate and host algae in their tissues.

cells._note: The one cell in this file with an explicit per-cell `value` (it equals the ladder position anyway, so the board still reads cleanly) and the one cell flagged lockValue — its points must never be altered by bonus randomization or any future mechanic (spec §4.1). Because lockValue is set, the bonus picker must skip it, so randomizable stays false here.
